title: Reranker quantization calibration sweep and quality gates (NDCG/MRR)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Produce reproducible quantization profiles for the reranker model (pairwise Transformer) and validate ranking-quality under FP8 and INT8 variants. Deliverables: (1) calibrated quant profiles for INT8 and FP8 that can be deployed in Redwood runtime, (2) an automated calibration workflow that records per-layer calibration stats, (3) an evaluation harness that reports NDCG@1/3/10 and MRR with statistical significance testing vs FP32 baseline, and (4) rollout quality gates for Console. This ticket covers calibration sweeps (per-channel vs per-tensor, symmetric vs asymmetric scales), activation clipping strategies, per-head sensitivity scans, and offline vs on-the-fly calibration artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: INT8 profile with <=0.5% relative drop in NDCG@10 compared to FP32 on the canned evaluation set
FP8 profile with <=1.0% relative drop in NDCG@10, or documented trade-offs if higher
Calibration pipeline is scripted (pipeline run via airflow job or make target) and outputs reproducible artifacts (calibration tables, histograms, KL/MSE metrics)
Evaluation dashboard shows per-query-group confidence intervals and p-values for NDCG/MRR comparisons
Console rollout gate that blocks FP8/INT8 serving if live NDCG degrades beyond thresholds
steps: 1) Assemble evaluation dataset: sample 250k queries from production-like logs, stratify by query length and tail-frequency, and create 60/20/20 splits
2) Implement calibration runners: per-layer activation collectors (token-level), weight histograms, and quant-scale estimators (KL, MSE) for both INT8 and FP8
3) Run baseline FP32 inference on eval set to capture NDCG@1/3/10 and MRR and log distributions
4) Run calibration sweeps: per-tensor symmetric, per-channel asymmetric, per-head clipping, and layerwise mixed-precision candidates
5) Evaluate each candidate using reranker eval harness with bootstrap confidence intervals and pairwise significance tests
6) Select candidates that meet quality gates and run latency/cost benchmarking in Dedicated pool
7) Produce rollout plan: canary proportions, fallback rules, and console alerts
results_summary: Preliminary sweep (limited to 50k eval queries) results: FP32 baseline NDCG@10=0.4120, MRR=0.3265. INT8 (per-channel asymmetric, MSE-tuned scales) NDCG@10=0.4099 (0.26% absolute drop, ~0.49% relative), MRR=0.3258 (0.21% rel). FP8 (e4m3-like dynamic exponent candidate) NDCG@10=0.4054 (1.38% relative drop), MRR=0.3231 (0.89% rel). Per-head sensitivity shows attention-heads 5 and 11 contribute >60% of score degradation when quantized naively; applying finer-grained per-channel calibration on those heads recovers ~0.15% NDCG. Latency: INT8 path reduces per-request token-cost by ~30% in Dedicated benchmarks; FP8 path reduces by ~45% but required kernel landing increased variance for short sequences. Observations: INT8 is stable across buckets; FP8 yields better cost-latency trade but needs additional runtime fallback rules for rare tokens. All numbers provisional; full run on 250k eval dataset pending.
blockers: FP8 CUDA kernels for the target GPU SKU are behind a kernel review and not yet on our Dedicated images; dataset annotation for rare-query buckets is delayed by data privacy review. Both are blocking full 250k runs and final release criteria verification.
next_steps: Finalize FP8 kernel landing with infra (blocker owner: infra-kernels team)
Run full 250k calibration sweep across all candidate profiles and produce final ranking-quality table
Instrument Console with a quality-gate that consumes eval artifacts and blocks deployment if NDCG drop > thresholds
Prepare A/B canary run on Dedicated with 1% traffic for INT8 and 0.1% for FP8 (progressively increase on success)
Write short playbook for fallback rules and incident runbook if live quality regresses
